subject: Marketplace: Harmonizing residency & retention across AWS/GCP/Azure (Q&A)
messages:
From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@acme-corp.com>
To: irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <procurements@cloudmarket.io>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace listing — residency + retention questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As we're working through Acme's marketplace onboarding, LegalOps asked for a concise mapping of where customer data lives (AWS/GCP/Azure) and how long we retain different artifacts (logs, request/response payloads, KV caches). Two specific asks:  

1) For customers who select "US" residency on the marketplace listing, can you confirm which cloud regions we map to for AWS/GCP/Azure and whether we have any cross-region backups?
2) For retention: what are default retention windows for (a) inference request/response logs, (b) KV cache/prefix cache, (c) observability traces? Also, what is the deletion workflow for a marketplace partner-initiated request?

I've attached our vendor intake spreadsheet and the SOC2 questionnaire for context (see attachment stub: acme_onboarding_sheet.xlsx, acme_soc2_questions.pdf). Can you point Acme Legal to a single place that summarizes the guarantees we can include in the Marketplace contract?

Appreciate it—if easier, we can schedule a 20-min sync.

Best,
Sandeep Rao
Head of Cloud Integrations
Acme Corp

From: irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, LegalOps <procurements@cloudmarket.io>
Date: 2027-04-19T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — residency + retention questions

Hi Sandeep — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; attaching a compact mapping spreadsheet (residency_mapping_v2.xlsx) that teams can include with the contract. I put the minimal legal-friendly phrasing you can copy into the marketplace listing.

Quick answers:  
- Region mapping (US residency):
  - AWS: us-east-2 or us-east-1 (primary: us-east-2; fallback to us-east-1 for capacity).
  - GCP: us-central1 (primary) with failover to us-east4 for burst isolation.
  - Azure: eastus2 (primary) with replication snapshot retained in westus2 for DR only (controlled by policy).
  - Cross-region backups: we maintain asynchronous metadata snapshots for disaster recovery. Personal data and customer payloads are not replicated outside chosen primary region except when required for critical DR—these snapshots are encrypted and accessible under strict controls.

- Default retention windows (Marketplace defaults; customers can request overrides during onboarding):
  - Inference request/response logs: 30 days by default (configurable to 90/180 for Enterprise customers via Dedicated/Private plans).
  - KV/cache (ephemeral prefix/kvcache): 7 days default for prefix cache; persistent KV entries for model session resumes are kept 30 days and then rotated out unless explicitly pinned.
  - Observability/tracing: 90 days aggregated metrics; 30 days raw traces.

- Deletion workflow for partner-initiated requests:
  1) Submit a deletion request via Marketplace ticket (we can embed a template).
  2) Ops verifies account & residency; triggers a targeted deletion job that removes request/response logs and expunges KV/prefix caches in the primary region.
  3) DR snapshots are marked for retention policy review and scrubbed per agreed SLA (default 45 days post-request).
  4) We provide a deletion confirmation artifact (signed statement + audit log export).

What I'm going to do next:  
- Share the attached residency_mapping_v2.xlsx that maps service components to AWS/GCP/Azure regions and lists which artifacts are replicated.
- Jordan will confirm the exact wording LegalOps should add to the marketplace product page and provide the HubSpot deal link for tracking.

If you want a single contract line: "Redwood Inference will ensure that customer content designated for US residency is stored and processed in the customer's selected US region(s) and that cross-region replication will only occur for disaster-recovery purposes under encryption and access controls." (We can tighten per legal ask.)

Let me know if Acme wants tighter retention (we can offer 90/90/180 as options on Dedicated).

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Partner Solutions (Marketplace)
Redwood Inference

2) Retention SLA options to list as toggles in the marketplace UI: Basic (30d logs / 7d cache / 30d traces), Advanced (90d logs / 30d cache / 90d traces), Enterprise (180d logs / 90d cache / 365d traces + manual deletion support).

Hi all — tagging in a concise legal clause and confirming SOC2 evidence attachment (acme_soc2_evidence.pdf stub). Below is language LegalOps approved for marketplace copy; it is intentionally non-technical and suitable for customer-facing pages.

Legal clause (marketplace):
"Redwood Inference processes and stores customer content in the geographic regions designated by the customer. For customers who select US residency, data will be stored and processed in US-based cloud regions on the selected provider. Cross-region replication is limited to encrypted disaster recovery snapshots and is performed only under explicit operational controls. Customers may request deletion of stored content and associated logs via the Marketplace support flow; Redwood will execute deletion and provide a confirmation artifact within the agreed SLA."

Deletion confirmation artifact: we will provide a signed PDF that includes the account identifier, deletion scope, timestamp, and audit trace IDs. Ops will retain minimal audit traces for compliance but these are tagged and stored under the customer retention policy and can be exported on request.

I'll let LegalOps confirm the exact retention numbers to publish, but the default options Jordan listed are acceptable from a compliance perspective. If Acme wants a custom retention/replication arrangement, we should include that in the Marketplace T&Cs as an addendum to the listing.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
